# ui::TextMeasurer

Header: `winui/render/Text.hpp`.

Measures text. The on-screen implementation measures with the real fonts, and the headless one (HeadlessTextMeasurer) uses a deterministic approximation. Because measurement sits behind this interface, layout runs without a window: [Element::measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) takes a measurer and passes it down the tree.

Call it through [MeasureContext::measurer](../tree/measure-context.md#measurer). The library implements it.

Parallel layout ([ParallelLayout](../tree/parallel-layout.md)) calls one measurer from several threads at once, so an implementation keeps no unsynchronized state: both shipped ones keep none at all.

Example: 
```cpp
// An element is handed the measurer when it is measured, and never keeps it:
class Caption : public ui::Element
{
protected:
    ui::Size measure_override(ui::Size available, const ui::MeasureContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::TextStyle style{.font_size = 14.0f, .wrapping = ui::TextWrapping::Wrap};
        // Wrapped to a bounded width; an unbounded one (ui::Unbounded) keeps it on one line.
        return context.measurer.measure_wrapped(text_, style, available.width);
    }

private:
    std::string text_;
};
```

## ~TextMeasurer

```cpp
virtual ~TextMeasurer() = default
```

## measure

```cpp
virtual TextMetrics measure(std::string_view text, const TextStyle& style) const = 0
```

One line, whatever `style.wrapping` says: the natural, unbroken extent of the run, in DIPs. `text` is UTF-8.

## measure_wrapped

```cpp
virtual TextMetrics measure_wrapped(std::string_view text, const TextStyle& style, float) const
```

The run broken into lines no wider than `max_width` per `style.wrapping`: the widest line's width and the height of all lines together. A width of 0 or less, an infinite one ([ui::Unbounded](../core/namespace-ui.md#unbounded)), or a NoWrap style, is [measure()](#measure). The default ignores wrapping altogether; both shipped measurers override it.
